```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
```

## 1. Introduction
This report investigates the off-label overprescription of GLP-1 receptor agonists (Semaglutide) for cosmetic weight loss, analyzing the financial motives and the resulting disproportionate adverse events.

```{r load_data}
cms_data <- read_csv("../processed/cms_volume_output.csv")
faers_data <- read_csv("../processed/faers_full_ml_data.csv")
meps_data <- read_csv("../processed/meps_financial_output.csv")
```

## 2. The Result: Medicare Part D Volume
Medicare Part D statutorily excludes weight-loss indications, so CMS volume reflects primarily diabetes use. Nonetheless, Semaglutide shows massive growth.

```{r volume_growth, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
ggplot(cms_data, aes(x = year, y = total_prescriptions / 1e6, color = generic_name, group = generic_name)) +
  geom_line(size = 1.5) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  labs(
    title = "Prescription Volume Trends (2020-2024)",
    subtitle = "Medicare Part D Total Claims (Primarily Diabetes Use)",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Total Prescriptions (Millions)",
    color = "Drug Cohort"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## 3. The Motive: Unit Economics
MEPS data reveals that the average cost per prescription for Semaglutide is vastly higher than standard controls like Metformin and Phentermine.

```{r financial_motive, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
meps_2024 <- meps_data %>% filter(year == 2024)

ggplot(meps_2024, aes(x = reorder(generic_name, avg_cost_per_prescription), y = avg_cost_per_prescription, fill = generic_name)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0("$", round(avg_cost_per_prescription, 0))), hjust = -0.2, size = 5) +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  labs(
    title = "Unit Economics Comparison",
    subtitle = "Average Cost per Prescription in 2024 (MEPS Weighted National Estimates)",
    x = "",
    y = "Average Cost per Prescription ($)",
    fill = "Drug Cohort"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## 4. Pharmacovigilance: Inappropriate Use Signals
When we isolate the cohort of patients taking these drugs specifically for "Weight Loss", Semaglutide shows a disproportionate rate of inappropriate use reports (off-label, counterfeit, medication errors).

```{r off_label_signal, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
misuse_summary <- faers_data %>%
  filter(grepl("Weight Loss", drug_and_indication)) %>%
  group_by(drug_and_indication) %>%
  summarise(
    total_cases = sum(total_cases),
    misuse_cases = sum(misuse_cases),
    pct_misuse = (misuse_cases / total_cases) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(misuse_summary, aes(x = reorder(drug_and_indication, pct_misuse), y = pct_misuse, fill = drug_and_indication)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(pct_misuse, 1), "%")), hjust = -0.2, size = 5) +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  labs(
    title = "Inappropriate Use & Administration Signals",
    subtitle = "Percentage of total cases reporting misuse, off-label, or counterfeit events",
    x = "",
    y = "Percentage of Total Cases (%)",
    fill = "Drug Cohort"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, max(misuse_summary$pct_misuse, na.rm=TRUE) * 1.2))
```

## 5. Limitations
FAERS is a spontaneous reporting system and cannot estimate incidence. Reporting is influenced by media attention, litigation, and product shortages (the Weber effect). The "off-label use" PT is coded from the same reported-use information used to define the indication stratum, so its association with the weight-loss stratum is partly definitional. We therefore treat these results as hypothesis-generating signals, not evidence of causal effects or of marketing-driven harm. "Weight loss" indications include on-label use (Wegovy, Phentermine), and our Semaglutide exposure includes compounded products that cannot be separated from manufactured ones. Medicare Part D statutorily excludes weight-loss indications, so CMS volume reflects primarily diabetes use. No direct measure of marketing exposure was available.
